analysis:
This batch is documentation only: a changelog entry, a new docs/architecture/addon-hold.md, an index link, an Autopilot busy-reason note (model-autopilot.md lines 182-184), and test instructions (docs/developer/test.md). No executable code is visible, so I found no concrete regression.

The docs describe a new local attack surface: an owner-only Unix socket `~/.darkbloom/runtime/addon.sock`. A signed add-on can use it to hold the provider. A hold sets status draining, unloads all models, persists across restart, and leaves routing without sending provider_drain. The documented controls are the peer policy (code requirement, hardened runtime, same user, add-on identifier equal to the verified signer), owner-only runtime files, a 30-600 s lease bounded by an ownership.lock probe, and `addon release --force` as an operator override. These bear on availability (T-010, T-029, T-057 class), TB-003 (local operator versus process) and TB-011 (App Attest worker kept alive). The hold does not touch serving authorization, encryption or attestation. The docs say the App Attest worker stays connected and that the hold does not block its recovery. A held provider still reports draining, so T-053 stale-authorization behavior is not visibly weakened. The prompt-cache threat T-041 is unaffected, since the hold only releases KV segments and unloads models.

The next pass should check the unreviewed Swift implementation. The paths named in the docs are provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Addon/AddonPeerPolicy.swift, AddonIPCServer.swift, AddonHoldStore.swift, ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift, ProviderDrain.swift and ProviderBusy.swift. Questions to check:
- Is the peer check effective? The tests (docs/developer/test.md, final paragraph) exercise it only negatively, with a test authenticator standing in for a real signed add-on.
- Are the socket and record permissions and the stale-socket handling safe?
- Can a same-user process bypass the signer check, for example through a PID-reuse race or an unsigned process?
- Can a hold with a permanent lock denial-of-service the provider? That is a local, same-user, operator-controlled risk.
- Does the coordinator-visible busy_addon string or busy metadata leak anything?

Coordinator handling of the busy fields ships separately and is outside the supplied evidence.
